# CV-Insight — Final Report

**Date:** 2026-08-04
**Version:** V2 (Schema v2: criteria_scores + rationales)
**Suite:** 387 tests passing | Benchmark mean 56.4 | Demo mean 56.2
**Metrics:** `models/week7_metrics.json` (regenerated by `scripts/week7_eval.py`)

---

## 1. What we built

An end-to-end **automatic CV evaluation, scoring, and ranking system**:

```
CV file → parser (PDF/DOCX/TXT/OCR) → section_splitter → extractor (rules + NER)
       → CVSchema (Pydantic) → scorer (rubric, criteria_scores + rationales)
       → suggester → classifier (TF-IDF + XGBoost) → matcher (JD ranking)
```

Three versions were delivered: **V1** (extract→score→suggest), **V2** (job-description
matching and multi-CV ranking), and a **Schema v2** (auditable criteria breakdown with
human-readable rationales). Extraction supports both a pure rule path and a fast
`Rule + NER` option (fine-tuned distilbert, CPU).

---

## 2. Evaluation metrics

Reproducible via `scripts/week7_eval.py`. All numbers below are current.

### 2.1 Classifier (quality label: Strong / Average / Weak)

TF-IDF on raw CV text, trained on ~4,500 labeled CVs, 80/20 stratified split.

| Model | Test accuracy | Weighted F1 |
|---|---|---|
| Majority-class baseline | 0.7346 | 0.6222 |
| Logistic Regression (TF-IDF) | 0.8581 | 0.8642 |
| **XGBoost (TF-IDF)** | **0.8765** | **0.8754** |

XGBoost is the trained classifier; the deployed classifier is the v3 hybrid
(`models/classifier_v3_hybrid_synth.pkl`, app load prefers it; `xgb_classifier.pkl`
remains as fallback).

### 2.2 Extraction — rule-based vs fine-tuned LLM (Qwen3-0.6B LoRA)

Ran both pipelines on the 10 demo CVs and scored each with the same rubric. LLM
skills are **grounded** (only in-text tokens kept) to remove hallucination.

| Path | Mean score | Wins vs rules |
|---|---|---|
| Rule-based | 53.6 | — |
| **Fine-tuned LLM (grounded)** | **65.6** | **10 / 10 (100%)**  |

Latency ~27.6 s/CV (CPU). Because that is far slower than real-time and heavy for the
1 GB Cloud tier, the **LLM path is kept as a research/batch option**; the shipped app
defaults to rules with the optional CPU `Rule + NER` tagger.

### 2.3 NER — span-extraction tagger (distilbert `models/ner-v1`)

Token-level metrics on the held-out test split (`ner_tags_test.jsonl`):

- Precision **0.998** / Recall **0.998** / **F1 0.998** (token-level)

> Caveat: train and test come from the same synthetic generated corpus, so this F1 is
> an **in-domain** figure, not cross-domain generalization. The tagger's real value is
> structural: it emits only spans present in the text (impossible to hallucinate) and
> is fast (~15 m/s) — ideal as a CPU `Rule + NER` app option. seqeval entity-level F1 on
> a real held-out corpus is future work.

**Entity-level (span) F1 (added 2026-08-05):** our hand-rolled seqeval-equivalent
span-level evaluation (`scripts/eval_ner_entity_level.py` → `models/ner_entity_level.json`)
reports **P=0.981 / R=0.995 / F1=0.988** on the in-domain test split — the token-level
figure modestly overstates real entity accuracy, but the tagger stays strong. On the real
demo/benchmark resumes, NER found 183 spans across 20 files; its spans are always in-text
by construction (only 7/183 "missing" under a strict verbatim check, and those are
span-joining/tokenization artifacts — comma-split skill lists, case/newline splits — not
hallucinated tokens).

### 2.4 Matcher / ranking

- **Spearman ρ = 0.314** (p=7.3e-13, n=500) between `semantic_score()` and the ATS
  dataset's **human ordinal label** (No/Potential/Good Fit) — an embedder-independent
  ground truth. This replaced the earlier misleading ρ=0.193 which compared against the
  dataset's jina-v2-derived `ats_score` (a different embedding model). The jina
  comparison (ρ=0.299) is now kept only as a labeled reference.
- **NDCG@5 = 0.98** on the controlled benchmark set (10 candidates, JD synthesized from
  the strongest CV, rubric score as relevance). This is the headline ranking metric.
- **Embedder (D):** default switched to `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` (env `CV_EMBEDDER`
  overrides). Direct ATS comparison: MiniLM ρ=0.259 → **bge-small 0.348** (bge-base
  0.260 but slower), so bge-small is the CPU-practical optimum.
- **Fine-tuned embedder (ConFit, 2026-08-05):** `scripts/train_matcher_confit.py`
  contrastively fine-tunes bge-small on the 6,241 `resume-job-description-fit` pairs →
  `models/matcher-confit`, **adopted as the default embedder** (`CV_EMBEDDER` overrides).
  ATS human-label ρ **0.314 → 0.436** (+39% rel); NDCG@5 **0.985** (no regression).
- **Learned weights (D):** `scripts/learn_ranker_weights.py` fits the semantic:skill
  ratio against human labels → semantic-dominant (best_w=1.0, ρ=0.338 vs 0.075 for the
  0.5 blend). Skill-overlap is noisy on unstructured ATS text; the ranker now accepts a
  `weights=` dict / `CV_RANK_WEIGHTS` env for tuned deployments.
- Remaining backlog: E (hybrid BM25) implemented 2026-08-05 (opt-in, default weight 0.0;
  see `docs/matcher_datasets_latency.md` §5); quantifying a nonzero hybrid default pending.

### 2.5 Extraction quality (rule path, benchmark)

`demo/benchmark/` — 10 reproducible scenario CVs targeting known failure modes:

| Stage | Benchmark mean |
|---|---|
| Baseline | 46.4 |
| After audit fixes | 53.6 |
| After follow-on hardenings (ORG-FP repair, project titles, aliases, date-first) | **56.4** |

Demo mean: **56.2**. Accumulated **+9.8 pts** on the benchmark, no regression on the
demo set. 387 tests pass; extraction entries/counts verified across all 10 scenarios.

## 3. Architecture

- **Parser** (`src/parser/`): 3-strategy PDF, DOCX tables-as-lines, TXT; OCR fallback
  (pytesseract + easyocr) with preprocessing and correction.
- **Section splitter** (`src/parser/section_splitter.py`): 80+ heading aliases →
  normalized `experience / skills / education / ...` dict.
- **Extractor** (`src/extractor/`): rules + spaCy NER + optional fine-tuned distilbert
  tagger (`ner_tag.py`); dataset adapters (`adapters.py`)
  for NETSOL/NER/ATS/classification.
- **Scorer** (`src/scorer/`): reads `config/rubric_config.json` (weights) and
  `config/default_criteria.json` (criterion list). Emits `criteria_scores` — an auditable
  list with `score / max_points / weight / method / rationale / overridden_by` — plus the
  legacy `section_scores` dict and `total_score`.
- **Suggester**: config-thresholded, template-based tips (no LLM).
- **Classifier**: TF-IDF vectorizer + `XGBoost` (+ `LogisticRegression` baseline).
- **Matcher** (`src/matcher/`): sentence-transformer embedder, cosine similarity, skill
  overlap, weighted ranker (0.5/0.3/0.2).
- **Schema** (`src/schema.py`): Pydantic `CVSchema`; V2 renamed `jd_match → match`
  (legacy `jd_match` still accepted on load + `jd_match` property alias kept).

---

## 4. Strengths & artifacts

- **Config-driven scoring** — no hardcoded weights; add/reorder a criterion in
  `default_criteria.json` and the score follows.
- **Auditable scores** — every criterion carries a human-readable rationale.
- **Hallucination-resistant** — rule + grounded-NER paths only emit in-text spans.
- **Reproducible benchmark** — `scripts/generate_benchmark_cvs.py` regenerates the set.
- Shipped models: `xgb_classifier.pkl`, `lr_baseline.pkl`,
  `classifier_v3_hybrid_synth.pkl` (deployed app classifier),
  `qwen3-0.6b-cv-lora-v2` (LLM LoRA), `ner-v1` (distilbert NER).

---

## 5. Remaining / Known limitations

- **Deployment:** Streamlit Community Cloud runs out of memory (1 GB RAM) with
  torch + easyocr; scanned-PDF OCR is disabled there. Text PDF/DOCX/TXT work. Fix is a
  Docker host (Render.com/Railway) or dropping easyocr on the Cloud tier.
- **NER F1 is in-domain**; a seqeval entity-level eval on real resumes is pending.
- **Matcher ρ** below aspirational target (embedding-model mismatch), not a product bug.
- **Bangla CV support** — designed (three-phase plan: English fine-tune → collect/translate
  Bangla CVs → native Onneshon / B-NER) but not built.
- **Company Mode / async batch / auth** — deferred (see `project_plan.md` Appendix A).

---

## 6. How to reproduce

```bash
pytest tests/                                   # 387 tests
python scripts/generate_benchmark_cvs.py        # regenerate demo/benchmark
python scripts/week7_eval.py                    # aggregate all metrics → models/week7_metrics.json
python scripts/vectorize_cvs.py                # retrain classifier
python scripts/gate_llm_vs_rules.py            # LLM vs rules comparison (needs GPU)
python scripts/gate_ner_vs_llm.py              # NER vs LLM vs rules
streamlit run app/app.py                        # launch the UI
```
